newsitem.title: INDIA: India PM said unlikely to unveil market steps.
newsitem.headline: India PM said unlikely to unveil market steps.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda is not expected to announce any measures to shore up capital markets in a speech in Bombay on Monday, a spokesman said.
Deve Gowda was scheduled to address The All India Association of Industries at 5 p.m. (1130 GMT) in the country's financial capital.
"The visit to Bombay is not connected to the capital markets," the spokesman said. "It has nothing to do with the capital markets."

Analysts and dealers in Bombay had said they were looking to Deve Gowda to unveil measures to boost capital markets and revive sagging industrial growth before leaving on January 31 for the World Economic Forum meeting in Davos, Switzerland.
Mounting anticipation about the package fuelled an early rally at Bombay bourses on Monday, with the key Bombay share index surging over three percent in early trade.

At 10.35 a.m. (0505 GMT) the 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange was up 3.02 percent or 103.72 points at 3,539.34. After hitting a three-year low on December 4, the BSE index soared 40 percent by mid-January.
But the rally has shown signs of tiring. The benchmark index ended last week down 13.27 points, or 0.39 percent, at 3,435.62.
Asked if a package of measures was due to be announced this week, the prime minister's spokesman said: "There are always a few things on the drawing board."
Analysts in Bombay had said some of the possible measures included allowing companies to buy back their shares to reduce equity overhang and scrapping taxes on shareholders' dividends.
Dealers had said the government might also raise the ceiling on foreign institutional holdings in State Bank of India, the country's largest commercial bank, to 24 percent from 20 percent.

Deve Gowda's cabinet was due to meet at 11 a.m. (0530 GMT) on Monday to take up a broadcast bill, government officials said. The Economic Times said the bill would limit foreign investors' stakes in television or radio ventures to 49 percent.

A Finance Ministry official reiterated that the government was not expected to announce a single package of measures before Deve Gowda and Finance Minister P. Chidambaram leave together for the Davos meeting.

"There has been a lot of misinterpretation on this," the official, who asked not to be named, said, citing newspaper reports that Deve Gowda had promised a package of measures before the end of January.

"There have been a lot of important decisions already announced," the official said, mentioning the recent publication of foreign investment guidelines by the Industry Ministry and the tax exemption for long-term capital gains on equity investments in infrastructure firms.
"These are signals that we are prepared to clean up our act, going step by step," the Finance Ministry official said.
